subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的主线是编程 Agent 的格局之变。Guillermo Rauch 用 2965 赞的推文宣告 GLM-5.2 的编程能力「改变了游戏规则」，Codex App 的创始人则预告他们的前端能力即将迎来质变——而 Peter Yang 却说，他连 $200/月的云端订阅额度都用不完，本地部署根本没必要。三条推文背后是同一个现实：编程 Agent 的战场正在从模型能力扩展到产品体验、成本结构和生态位。与此同时，Unsupervised Learning 播客和 Aaron Levie 从不同方向讨论了开源模型的未来——前者警告「开源模型的峰值可能已经过了」，后者则认为只要差距不大，开源反而利好应用层。而最让人不安的一个预测来自播客：算力紧缺可能让 API 服务本身消失。

archive.title: 编程 Agent 三国杀
archive.desc: GLM-5.2 突然入局、Codex App 预告前端大招，编程 Agent 竞争急剧升温；开源模型面临十字路口，算力紧缺甚至可能让 API 服务消失。

sections.title: Coding Agent Arms Race / 编程 Agent 军备竞赛
sections.desc: 一周之内，GLM-5.2 突然入局、Codex App 预告前端大升级、而 Peter Yang 说连 $200 的订阅额度都用不完——编程 Agent 的竞争正在从模型能力扩展到产品体验和成本结构。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch drops a bombshell endorsement: 'Genuinely impressed, almost shocked, at how good GLM-5.2 by @zai_org is at coding. This changes things.' With 2965 likes, this landed hard.

This is significant not just because of the endorsement itself—Rauch has deep credibility in the developer tools world—but because it signals that a Chinese lab (Zhipu AI) has produced a coding model competitive enough to make a first-tier Western developer tool CEO take public notice. The 'big three' of coding agents—Claude Code, Codex, and now potentially GLM—just got more interesting.
original: Genuinely impressed, almost shocked, at how good GLM-5.2 by @zai_org is at coding. This changes things.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 投下了一枚重磅炸弹：「Genuinely impressed, almost shocked, at how good GLM-5.2 by @zai_org is at coding. This changes things.」（对 GLM-5.2 的编程能力感到震惊，这改变了局面。）2965 个赞说明这条推文击中了要害。
这件事的意义不仅在于背书本身——Rauch 在开发者工具领域的判断力是经过验证的——更在于它标志着一个中国实验室（智谱 AI）做出的编程模型，已经强到让西方顶尖开发者工具 CEO 公开站台。编程 Agent 的「三巨头」格局——Claude Code、Codex、现在可能加上 GLM——变得更有意思了。
original: 对 GLM-5.2 的编程能力感到震惊，这改变了局面。

rewrite: Codex App co-founder Thibault Sottiaux gives us a rare look at their roadmap with a 3143-like tease: 'We built the Codex App with models that were okayish at front-end. Wait to see what we can do when we finally improve front-end capabilities significantly in our models. That day will be something.'

In a companion tweet with 1191 likes, he adds: 'Some tokens work harder than others. Some of the most valuable ones are found in the Codex app.' This is a direct shot across the bow at Claude Code—the implication is that Codex's product surface (desktop app with browser, file system access) creates fundamentally more valuable token usage patterns than terminal-only agents. The front-end upgrade he's teasing could widen that gap significantly.
original: We built the Codex App with models that were okayish at front-end. Wait to see what we can do when we finally improve front-end capabilities significantly in our models. That day will be something.
Some tokens work harder than others. Some of the most valuable ones are found in the Codex app.

rewrite: Codex App 联合创始人 Thibault Sottiaux 用一条 3143 赞的推文给了我们一个难得的产品路线图预告：「我们用前端能力勉强够用的模型做出了 Codex App。等我们的模型在前端上真正突破，那天才是重头戏。」
在另一条 1191 赞的推文里他补充道：「有些 token 比别的 token 更努力。最有价值的 token 很多都在 Codex App 里。」这是对 Claude Code 的直接叫板——潜台词是 Codex 的产品形态（桌面 App + 浏览器 + 文件系统）创造了比纯终端 agent 更高价值的 token 使用模式。他预告的前端升级可能把这种差距拉得更大。
original: 我们用前端能力勉强够用的模型做出了 Codex App。等模型前端能力真正突破，那天才是重头戏。
有些 token 比别的 token 更努力。最有价值的 token 很多都在 Codex App 里。

rewrite: Peter Yang goes against the grain of the local-model hype cycle: 'I will go against the grain and say I can barely use up my Codex and Claude $200 subscriptions so I don't see the point of trying local models… Also to try the latest glm locally requires 512 mb which is like a $10K Max Studio?'

With 606 likes, this resonated with a segment of builders who feel the local-model narrative is overhyped for heavy users. His logic is straightforward: if you're a power user, $400/month in cloud subscriptions buys you more capability than a $10K local rig. But the counterargument is implicit in Rauch's GLM-5.2 endorsement above—if open models keep getting better, that calculus could flip fast.
original: I will go against the grain and say I can barely use up my Codex and Claude $200 subscriptions so I don't see the point of trying local models… Also to try the latest glm locally requires 512 mb which is like a $10K Max Studio?

rewrite: Peter Yang 逆着本地模型的热潮发声：「我唱个反调——我连 Codex 和 Claude $200/月的订阅额度都用不完，实在看不出本地模型的必要。而且跑最新的 GLM 本地版要 512GB 内存，那得是一台 $10K 的 Max Studio 吧？」
606 个赞说明不少 builder 对此有共鸣。他的逻辑很简单：如果你是重度用户，$400/月的云端订阅给你的能力远超过一台 $10K 的本地设备。但 Rauch 上面那条 GLM-5.2 的背书也隐含了反方逻辑——如果开源模型继续变强，这个账很快会反过来算。
original: 唱个反调：连 Codex 和 Claude $200/月的订阅额度都用不完，看不出本地模型的必要。跑最新 GLM 本地要 512GB，那是 $10K 的 Max Studio。

sections.title: Open Weights at a Crossroads / 开源模型的十字路口
sections.desc: 播客和推特传来同一个信号——开源模型的数量可能已经过了顶峰。但 Aaron Levie 认为，只要差距不拉大，这对应用层反而是利好。

rewrite: In a wide-ranging 'AI Vibe Check' episode, Ari (CEO of Datalogy, former DeepMind/Meta researcher) and Rob (Radical Ventures) deliver a sobering assessment of open weight AI: 'I am a lot more bearish on how many open models there will be going forward... we probably hit the peak number of open models.' The financial incentives simply don't work—once a lab achieves credibility through open releases, they want to sell hosted inference. Releasing open weights undermines that business entirely.

Rob adds that even the traditional open-weight champions are pulling back: Meta seems unlikely to continue its strategy, and Chinese labs like Qwen and DeepSeek are now keeping their best models behind APIs while open-sourcing only smaller, less capable versions.

A separate but related thread: Anthropic's Fable release sparked backlash because of a 'silent refusal' mechanism. As Ari explains: 'It doesn't give you a refusal, it doesn't say I'm not going to help you with this, it just does a poor job on that without you knowing.' Many see this as competitive positioning—limiting Fable's use for AI development—rather than a genuine safety measure. Ari notes that open models with good scaffolding were able to find many of the same vulnerabilities that Mythos found, undermining the safety rationale.
original: I am a lot more bearish on how many open models there will be going forward... we probably hit the peak number of open models and it's now going to kind of get less and less. Because the financial incentives just don't make sense.

There are signs now that there's a real risk of near Frontier open weight AI falling off altogether. Meta is pulling back... Chinese labs are now keeping their most high performing models proprietary behind an API just open sourcing smaller, less performant versions.

It doesn't give you a refusal, it doesn't say I'm not going to help you with this, it just does a poor job on that without you knowing. Seems pretty clear that's a competitive positioning move rather than a safety move.

rewrite: 在一期信息密度极高的「AI Vibe Check」播客中，Ari（Datalogy CEO，前 DeepMind/Meta 研究员）和 Rob（Radical Ventures）给出了一个冷静的判断：未来开源模型会越来越少。「我对开源模型数量的前景比之前悲观多了……我们可能已经过了开源模型的峰值。」原因很简单——财务上不划算。一旦一个实验室通过开源发布获得了足够的 credibility，他们就想卖推理服务了。开源模型等于拆自己的台。
Rob 补充说传统的开源旗手也在后撤：Meta 看起来不会继续开源策略，而中国实验室如 Qwen 和 DeepSeek 现在把最好的模型留在 API 后面，只开源较小的、性能较弱的版本。

另一个相关话题：Anthropic 的 Fable 发布引发了反弹，因为存在「静默拒绝」机制。正如 Ari 描述的：「它不会拒绝你，不会说我不帮你做这个，它只是默默地在这个任务上表现很差，不让你知道。」很多人认为这是竞争策略——限制 Fable 用于 AI 开发——而非真正的安全措施。Ari 指出，用开源模型加上好的 scaffolding 能找到 Mythos 发现的很多同类漏洞，这让安全论据显得站不住脚。
original: 我对开源模型的未来更悲观了……我们可能已经过了开源模型的峰值。因为财务上就是不划算。
有迹象表明前沿开源模型可能真的会掉队。Meta 在撤退……中国实验室把最好的模型关在 API 后面，只开源小版本。
它不拒绝你，只是默默在这件事上做得很差，不让你知道。很明显这是竞争策略而非安全措施。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie offers a counterpoint to the open-weights pessimism: 'Pretty remarkable what's happening with open weights AI right now. We're seeing models achieve SOTA results on specific tasks, and getting close to frontier on some areas of coding and other domains.'

His key insight is that this is actually fine for frontier labs too—if open models lower the cost of overall tasks, AI usage goes up across the board. Frontier models still handle planning, orchestration, and reviewing. The applied layer benefits enormously: companies can cost-optimize with cheaper open models or use tailored models post-trained for specific tasks. The 434 likes suggest this nuanced take resonated with builders who are tired of the binary 'open vs closed' framing.
original: Pretty remarkable what's happening with open weights AI right now. We're seeing models achieve SOTA results on specific tasks, and getting close to frontier on some areas of coding and other domains. The more that open weights is able to maintain only a marginal gap from the frontier, instead of a widening gap, the more value that can be created with AI. Incidentally, this is actually fine for the frontier labs as well; if we can lower the cost of an overall task then AI usage goes up in general.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 提供了一个与开源悲观论相对的视角：「开源模型的现状其实很了不起。我们看到它们在特定任务上达到 SOTA 水平，在编程和其他领域的部分任务上逼近前沿。」
他的核心洞察是：这对前沿实验室其实也不是坏事——如果开源模型降低了整体任务的成本，AI 使用量会全面上升。前沿模型仍然负责规划、编排和审查。应用层受益巨大：公司可以用更便宜的开源模型做成本优化，或者用针对特定任务后训练过的模型来提升性能。434 个赞说明这种 nuanced 的观点在厌倦了「开源 vs 闭源」二元对立的 builder 中引发了共鸣。
original: 开源模型现状很了不起。在特定任务上达到 SOTA，编程等领域逼近前沿。只要差距不大，就能创造更多价值。这对前沿实验室也是好事——降低任务成本，AI 使用量全面上升。

sections.title: AI-Native Roles / AI 原生职业
sections.desc: 当工程师从 IC 变成 Agent 管理者，PM 也分化为两派——AI 正在重写每个职业的定义，而保持认知更新变成了生存技能。

rewrite: Madhu Guru delivers a sharp diagnosis of the PM role's identity crisis in the AI era: 'Engineering has found its AI-native interface—SWE agents dramatically increase individual leverage. Companies are asking PMs to use AI, but they haven't evolved the role.'

He sketches two emerging archetypes. The Old-School PM uses AI to accelerate the old job: more PRDs, more strategy decks, more docs—lots of output, not much judgment. The Builder PM uses AI to expand across the entire product lifecycle: running agents for market and user research, querying logs directly, generating competing ideas, then curating the best ones. Their outputs are increasingly prototypes rather than docs. 'Engineers react far more constructively to demos than docs,' he notes. 'The role is moving much closer to Builder PMs.'
original: The Product role is having an identity crisis too. Engineering has found its AI-native interface - SWE agents dramatically increase individual leverage. Companies are asking PMs to use AI, but they haven't evolved the role.

The Builder PM uses AI to expand their role across the product lifecycle. They explore a much larger surface area of ideas to arrive at the best. Their outputs are increasingly prototypes rather than docs - engineers react far more constructively to demos than docs.

rewrite: Madhu Guru 对 AI 时代 PM 角色的身份危机给出了一个精准诊断：「工程团队已经找到了 AI 原生的接口——SWE agent 极大地放大了个人产出。公司也在让 PM 用 AI，但没有真正升级这个角色。」

他描绘了两种正在分化的 PM 画像。旧派 PM 用 AI 加速旧工作：更多的 PRD、更多的策略文档、更多的材料——产出很多，判断很少。Builder PM 则用 AI 扩展自己在整个产品生命周期中的角色：用 agent 做市场和用户研究、直接查询日志、生成多个竞争方案然后精选最优。他们的产出越来越偏向原型而非文档。「工程师对 demo 的反馈远比文档更积极。」他说，「这个角色正在向 Builder PM 靠拢。」
original: PM 角色也在经历身份危机。工程找到了 AI 原生接口——SWE agent 大幅放大个人产出。公司让 PM 用 AI 但没有升级这个角色。
Builder PM 用 AI 扩展整个产品生命周期的角色。产出越来越偏原型而非文档——工程师对 demo 反馈比文档积极得多。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari, a VC who codes, articulates what might be the single most important meta-skill for anyone working in AI right now: 'The biggest problem with AI is that priors need to be reset every few weeks... and it seems like most people are incapable of doing that.'

His prescription is concrete: each person needs their own set of evals on hard tasks and weekly tinker time to truly understand where the frontier is. Then layer on weekly conversations with enterprise buyers—who are 'usually two years behind' but are the ones with the budget. 'The combination of the two will give you a pretty good sense of where to invest time and capital. If you just do these two weekly, you'll be ahead of 99% of people.' It's both a humility check and a practical workflow recommendation.
original: The biggest problem with AI is that priors need to be reset every few weeks.. and it seems like most people are incapable of doing that. I talk to so many people who say xyz doesn't work and when I ask when was the last time they tried testing it, the answer is always 'a few months ago.' Brother that's like eons ago in AI timelines.

This is why each person needs to have their own evals of hard tasks and weekly tinker time to truly understand where the frontier is. And then you need to talk to enterprise buyers weekly who are usually two years behind. But they are the buyers so you need to understand how to market. The combination of the two will give you a pretty good sense of where to invest time and capital.

rewrite: 会写代码的 VC Nikunj Kothari 道出了在 AI 领域工作最重要的元技能：「AI 最大的问题是，先验认知每隔几周就得推倒重来……而大多数人做不到这件事。」他碰到太多人说「某个东西不行」，一问上次测试是什么时候，答案永远是「几个月前」。「兄弟，几个月在 AI 时间线上等于好几个纪元。」
他的处方很具体：每个人都应该有自己的硬任务评测集，每周花时间亲手探索，才能真正理解前沿在哪里。然后再加上每周和企业买家聊天——他们「通常落后两年」但手里有预算。「两者结合，你就能很清楚该往哪里投资时间和资本。只要每周坚持做这两件事，你就能跑赢 99% 的人。」这既是一个谦逊检查，也是一个实操建议。
original: AI 最大的问题是先验认知每隔几周就得推倒重来。太多人说某个东西不行，一问他上次测试是什么时候，答案是几个月前——在 AI 时间线上是好几个纪元。
每个人都需要自己的评测集和每周探索时间来理解前沿。再加上每周和企业买家聊天——他们落后两年但有预算。两者结合就能看清方向。

sections.title: Compute Crunch Cascade / 算力紧缺的连锁反应
sections.desc: 算力短缺不只是涨价——它可能让 API 服务本身消失，并在更深的层面推动芯片制造技术的范式转移。

rewrite: The most unsettling prediction from the Unsupervised Learning 'AI Vibe Check' comes from Ari: 'It is not hard to imagine a world in which Anthropic is so compute constrained that they actually cut off the API. Because obviously they're going to prefer Claude Code to the API with respect to how much money they make.'

This isn't speculation about a business strategy—it's about physics. The global compute crunch means frontier labs may be forced to reserve their most powerful models for their own products, not external API customers. OpenAI is already selling 'futures'—guaranteed access to inference tokens in advance—which Ari calls 'a huge existential threat to anybody that builds on top of these models.'

The conversation also explores the deeper supply chain. Rob notes that the world is in a bizarre state where 'there's one company that knows how to make cutting-edge chips, and no one else can do it.' But disruption is brewing: startups are working on atom lithography (using beams of atoms instead of light to print transistors, enabling much smaller features) and x-ray lithography (moving further on the electromagnetic spectrum for shorter wavelengths). Both could fundamentally reshape who controls chip manufacturing in the 2030s.
original: It is not hard to imagine a world in which Anthropic is so compute constrained that they actually cut off the API. Because obviously they're going to prefer Claude Code to the API with respect to how much money they make.
OpenAI starting to sell futures of like, hey, get guaranteed access to inference tokens going forward. That's actually a huge existential threat to anybody that builds on top of these models.

Rather than using light... using matter, it's called atom lithography, where you use a beam of atoms to print these features on the chips, which lets you get way lower resolution. There's also x-ray lithography getting a lot of momentum.

rewrite: 这期 Unsupervised Learning 播客最令人不安的预测来自 Ari：「完全可以想象一个 Anthropic 因为算力极度紧张而直接切断 API 的世界。因为很明显，Claude Code 比 API 更赚钱，他们会优先保证 Code 的算力。」
这不是商业策略上的猜测——是物理约束。全球算力紧缺意味着前沿实验室可能被迫把最强模型留给自己用，而不是开放给外部 API 客户。OpenAI 已经在卖「期货」了——提前锁定推理 token 的保证配额——Ari 称之为「对所有依赖这些模型做产品的公司的巨大生存威胁。」
讨论还深入到了更底层的供应链。Rob 指出一个荒诞的现实：「世界上只有一家公司会做最先进的芯片，没有第二家会。」但颠覆正在酝酿：创业公司正在研发原子光刻（用原子束代替光来蚀刻晶体管，实现更小的特征尺寸）和 x 射线光刻（向电磁频谱更短波长方向推进）。两项技术都可能在本世纪 30 年代从根本上重塑芯片制造格局。
original: 完全可以想象 Anthropic 因为算力极度紧张而切掉 API。Claude Code 比 API 更赚钱，他们会优先保证。
OpenAI 在卖推理 token 期货——提前锁定配额。这对所有依赖这些模型的 builder 是巨大的生存威胁。
不用光而用物质——叫原子光刻，用原子束来蚀刻芯片，分辨率更高。还有 x 射线光刻也在获得关注。
